# Orphaned Primary Pending Delivery Repair

<!-- spec-coder:artifact-v1 spec -->

## Problem Statement

The deployed delivery Ring can accumulate unclaimed historical Primary Main
`session_status` updates after their owning Binding becomes orphaned or
archived. Production evidence showed 4,312 pending rows for one orphaned pane
scope, all targeting the same stale `primary-main` projection. A preceding
uncertain Ring-claim quarantine must remain protected, but these pending rows
have not attempted an external effect and cannot become valid targets again.
The resulting rows inflate `pendingOutbox` and `waitingBehindScope` and keep
periodic refill/recovery work active.

## Solution

Add a bounded, transactionally revalidated Ring-maintenance path that
terminalizes only unclaimed, no-effect pending Primary Main session-status
updates whose exact durable owner is orphaned, archived, or closed. The path
records a dismissal recovery audit, advances the affected scope checkpoint,
and wakes the scope after commit. It never releases or rewrites an uncertain
quarantine and never calls Gateway/Lark.

## User Stories

### SCN-1: Retire pending updates for an invalid Primary owner

During startup or periodic bounded Ring recovery, an unclaimed pending
`primary-main` `session_status` update whose exact owner is orphaned, archived,
or closed is dismissed as stale. The transition is durable, audited, and the
scope becomes eligible for the next remaining durable head without an
external delivery.

### SCN-2: Preserve an uncertain external-effect quarantine

When the same scope contains a dead-letter head with `effect_certainty`
`unknown` and an active `conflict_isolated` quarantine, maintenance may retire
later no-effect pending updates, but must leave the uncertain head, its
quarantine, and its human-review/recovery state unchanged.

### SCN-3: Lose a concurrent claim safely

If a candidate is claimed, checkpointed, linked to a prerequisite/recovery, or
otherwise changes between discovery and the maintenance transaction, the
transaction dismisses nothing for that candidate and leaves it recoverable by
the normal Ring path.

## Implementation Decisions

### INV-1: Only no-effect orphaned Primary Main rows are dismissible

The maintenance predicate requires the exact owner generation and session
epoch, Primary `session_status` identity, `pending` state, zero attempts, no
claim, no gateway/card checkpoint, no delivered message, no active recovery or
prerequisite, and an owner lifecycle/attachment state proving it can no
longer receive the update. If an active attached replacement Binding already
owns the same workspace/pane, the old row remains pending for authoritative
replacement projection. Uncertain effect rows and active quarantines are not
released by this change.

### INV-2: Dismissal is one local atomic transition

For each accepted row, the SQLite transaction changes the outbound row to
`dismissed`, inserts or updates its `delivery_recoveries` audit with a stable
orphan-retirement action, advances the delivery checkpoint from the new
terminal prefix, and queues a scope wake. A concurrent state change produces
no partial transition.

### INV-3: Bounded maintenance converges without Gateway work

Each maintenance invocation processes a bounded number of candidate rows and
returns affected scopes to the existing Ring recovery loop. Repeated passes
eventually drain a finite orphaned pending backlog. The operation has zero
Gateway/Lark calls and does not create replacement deliveries.

### ARCH-1: Prepared-delivery store owns the retirement predicate

`SqlitePreparedDeliveryStore` owns the durable owner/effect proof, transaction,
audit, checkpoint, and scope-wake mutation. `RingDeliveryEngine` continues to
own scheduling and bounded recovery invocation; it does not duplicate the
predicate or mutate SQLite directly. Existing ports and maintenance result
shapes are extended only as needed for affected-scope continuation.

### ARCH-2: Existing quarantine semantics remain authoritative

An uncertain claim-expiry head remains an authoritative blocker and active
quarantine. This repair handles only later pending rows that are provably
stale because their owner is invalid; it does not introduce conflict bypass,
uncertain-effect replay, age-based purge, or human-review policy changes.

## Testing Decisions

References: SCN-1, SCN-2, SCN-3, INV-1, INV-2, INV-3, ARCH-1, ARCH-2

Extend the existing real SQLite `prepared-delivery-store` seam with a
production-shaped orphaned Primary Main backlog: one invalid owner, many
unclaimed same-conflict session-status rows, and an uncertain quarantined
predecessor. Assert bounded dismissal, recovery audit, checkpoint/wake
effects, unchanged quarantine, and zero Gateway work. Add rollback and
concurrent-claim fixtures. Exercise the Ring recovery orchestration to prove
the bounded maintenance result is consumed without a global unbounded scan.
Run the existing focused Ring/store suites, typecheck, build, architecture
checks, and the full Vitest suite during delivery.

## Out of Scope

This change does not release or dismiss uncertain-effect heads, bypass active
conflict isolation for a new delivery, retry or recreate stale CardKit
targets, alter the three-attempt policy, purge arbitrary old outbox rows,
change SQLite schema, edit live SQLite, deploy, install, or restart services.
The separate risk that a candidate-scope query can scan a very large duplicate
run remains a follow-up unless a later approved design expands this scope.

## Further Notes

Workspace: `<repo-root>/.trae/worktrees/fix-ring-delivery-recovery`.

changes: none. The prior Gate 1 decision approved the bounded orphaned-pending
retirement design. No live data was modified.
